messages:
maria (People Ops): Thanks everyone — quick post-all-hands follow-up thread for the Q&A items we didn't finish. Drop short questions about reviews, leveling, promos, comp, and benefits and we'll triage to the right person. TL;DR: calibration window = 2024-05-08 to 2024-05-15, manager confirmations due 5/08, retro pay target 2024-06-01.

kevin (IC): Question — if my manager and I disagree on level rec (e.g., they put me at L3 but I think I'm L4), what's the exact path? Do we escalate? :thinking_face:

maria (People Ops): Good one. Short answer: managers submit their recommendation, then calibration happens across managers + HR. If there's a disagreement you can ask your manager to flag examples in the calibration form; if still unresolved, HR will schedule a calibration follow-up with the manager and a peer manager. Appeals are separate (post-calibration) — we can explain the appeals timeline if needed.

kevin (IC): Helpful — can a PM/eng peer submit feedback to support my case during calibration?

jordan (Eng Manager): Yes — peers can add written input into the calibration packet. Olivia and I both use the "peer evidence" doc link in the kit. Try to keep examples focused on impact + outcomes, not just tasks.

olivia (Manager): Adding: managers, please attach 2–3 concrete artifacts (PRs, RFCs, metrics) to support any level-up recs. The calibration rubric is lightweight but evidence-driven.

samir (VP Product): Quick ask on roadmap: will promotion pacing change for product teams given recent hiring? Curious because product hires joined mid-cycle.

maria (People Ops): Mid-cycle hires — comp and leveling for hires who started after the review snapshot date are handled case-by-case. Short rule: if they joined <30 days before snapshot, they typically get evaluated next cycle; exceptions can be submitted with manager rationale. For comp adjustments tied to promotions outside the cycle, managers submit a comp-change case and we'll review.

peopleops-bot: Resource pinned -> /handbook/reviews/calibration-guidelines (doc) and /forms/appeals-request (form).

kevin (IC): Thanks — one more: retro pay (promos effective 4/1) — will that show on the 6/01 payroll or individual adjustments?

maria (People Ops): Retro pay for promotions approved in this cycle is scheduled for the 2024-06-01 payroll. If payroll misses anything, ops will notify affected employees.

jordan (Eng Manager): Manager ask: is there an exception path for temporary market adjustments (comp hotspots) that need immediate fixes pre-commit? We have an offer acceptance case that looks misaligned now.

maria (People Ops): Yes — managers can open a "comp hotspot" case. We prioritize hires near offer or retention risk. Use the comp-case form and mark as urgent; include current offer, recommended range, and business justification.

amy (CEO): Appreciate the detailed ops work here. Two quick notes: 1) We want fairness and transparency — if something feels inconsistent please flag it openly. 2) Leadership will review calibration results and any systemic skews before final approvals.

kevin (IC): Appreciate the clarity — will peopleops publish a small FAQ summarizing timelines + appeal steps?

maria (People Ops): Yes — I'll draft a 1-pager FAQ and drop it in #announcements + the handbook by EOD tomorrow. If you have specific Qs, DM me or reply here. :raised_hands:

samir (VP Product): Thanks — and if product leadership can get a bulleted list of required artifacts for level-ups, I'll forward to PM leads.

maria (People Ops): Will do. Tagging: @samir, @jordan, @olivia — we'll sync on artifacts list and include examples in the handbook doc.

peopleops-bot: Calendar reminder posted: Calibration close 2024-05-15 17:00 PT.

amy (CEO): Thanks everyone. Short reminder: managers please block time for calibration reviews — it makes a huge difference.
